verses.text: Paul, an apostle—not sent by people or appointed through a human being, but through Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised Jesus from the dead—
and all the brothers and sisters with me, to the churches in Galatia:
Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from this present evil age, in keeping with the will of our God and Father.
To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I'm shocked that you're turning away so quickly from the one who called you by Christ's grace and following a different message.
There's no other Good News. Some people are confusing you and trying to twist Christ's Good News.
But even if we—or an angel from heaven—preach a different message than the one we preached to you, let them be condemned.
We've said it before, and I'll say it again: if anyone preaches a different message than the one you received, let them be condemned.
Am I trying to win people's approval or God's? Am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I wouldn't be Christ's servant.
Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that the Good News I preached didn't come from a human source.
I didn't receive it from a person or get taught it by one. It came through a revelation from Jesus Christ.
You've heard how I used to live in Judaism: I persecuted God's church viciously and tried to destroy it.
I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my own age and people, because I was even more devoted to my ancestors' traditions.
But God, who set me apart before I was born and called me by his grace,
was pleased to reveal his Son in me so I could preach him among the Gentiles. I didn't immediately consult with anyone,
or go to Jerusalem to see those who were apostles before me. Instead, I went to Arabia, then returned to Damascus.
After three years, I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas and stayed with him for fifteen days.
I didn't see any other apostles—only James, the Lord's brother.
I'm telling you the truth before God; I'm not lying about what I'm writing.
After that, I went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
The churches in Judea that are in Christ still didn't know me personally.
They had only heard, ‘The man who once persecuted us is now preaching the faith he once tried to destroy.’
And they praised God because of me.
